name: MATH
summary: Competition mathematics problems in seven subjects and five difficulty levels, each with a step-by-step solution that ends in a boxed final answer.

protocol.v: exact match of the final answer in \boxed{} after normalization: equivalent fraction forms, optional units, spaces ignored, 0.5 equal to 1/2, factor order ignored
protocol.loc: Section 3.1, Formatting and Automatically Assessing Generated Answers

data_hash.loc: the parquet of 12,500 problems of the mirror that the README of hendrycks/math links at commit 985bdc1, hashed here on 2026-11-15; the official MATH.tar returned HTTP 403

versions.name: MATH (test set)

data.location: MATH.tar linked from the README of github.com/hendrycks/math until 2025; now the mirror qwedsacf/competition_math on Hugging Face, which merges train and test

protocol.scorer: exact match of the boxed final answer after the normalization of modeling/math_equivalence.py (is_equiv)
protocol.unit: solved problems / all problems

human_baseline.note: a three-time IMO gold medallist on 20 random test problems in one hour; the university students tested solved 8 to 18 of 20 (Section 3.1)

versions.known_issues: hendrycks/competition_math on Hugging Face is disabled and the official MATH.tar returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-15, so reports may use different copies; lightman-2023-lets-verify-step moved 4,500 test problems into the training data of PRM800K and evaluates on the other 500 (MATH-500), so a score on MATH-500 is not a score on this version; 2 geometry problems of train have the level 'Level ?'

versions.name: MATH Level 5

derived_from.rule: the 1,324 problems of level 5 of the test set

data.location: the level 5 problems of the test split of the mirror EleutherAI/hendrycks_math (1,324 problems, counted on 2026-11-15); Epoch AI's runs read tadamcz/hendrycks___competition_math, which is not public

protocol.scorer: Epoch AI's runs: zero-shot, the answer on a last line 'ANSWER: $ANSWER', 8 runs a model, and three scorers: normalized string match, sympy equivalence, and gemini-1.5-flash-002 judging equivalence; the hub's column 'Best score (across scorers)' is the best of the three, the plots use the model judge (epoch-2026-math-level-5, Methodology)
protocol.unit: solved problems / 1,324

versions.known_issues: Epoch AI's log viewer is not available for MATH Level 5 because of copyright discussions (epoch.ai/benchmarks/about); the input data of Epoch AI's runs could not be checked against the official test set

name: ARC-AGI
summary: Grid puzzles in which a system infers a transformation from a few input and output examples and applies it to a new input, testing skill acquisition from little data.

protocol.v: a task is solved when the output grids of all its test inputs are exactly right, with 3 trials for each test input

data_hash.loc: a manifest of data/evaluation hashed here on 2026-11-15: one line '<sha256 of the file>  <file name>' a file, sorted by name, then the sha256 of the manifest

versions.name: ARC-AGI-1 (public evaluation set)

size.loc: 400 files with 419 test inputs, counted here on 2026-11-15

data.location: data/evaluation of github.com/fchollet/ARC-AGI at commit 399030444e0ab0cc8b4e199870fb20b863846f34 (the data is the same at release v1.0.2)

protocol.scorer: exact match of each output grid; 3 trials a test input in the 2019 paper, 2 attempts a test input in the ARC Prize (chollet-2024-arc-prize-2024, Section 1)
protocol.unit: solved tasks / all tasks

human_baseline.note: the share of public evaluation tasks that at least one Mechanical Turk worker of an NYU study solved, not a mean (chollet-2024-arc-prize-2024, Section 1.1)

versions.known_issues: the private set of 200 tasks of 2019 became a semi-private and a private set of 100 tasks each (chollet-2024-arc-prize-2024, Section 1.1); the public evaluation set is easier than the private one, about 10,000 scores on the private set have been revealed, and 49% of it was solved by at least one team of 2020 (chollet-2025-arc-agi-2, Section 2); release v1.0.2 of 2024-06-21 fixed 2 training and 9 evaluation tasks

name: LMArena
summary: Crowdsourced arenas where a user sends one prompt to two anonymous models and votes for the better answer; the votes are fitted to a rating for each model.

protocol.v: a user chats with two anonymous models side by side and votes for the better one

versions.name: LMArena text

data.location: lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset on Hugging Face, config text, splits latest and full

protocol.scorer: a Bradley-Terry rating fitted to the votes of the arena's users between two anonymous models, with a confidence interval; text chat, without style control
protocol.unit: rating; comparable only inside one leaderboard snapshot of this arena

name: GSM8K
summary: Grade school math word problems written by people, each with a worded solution and a final number, testing the multi-step arithmetic reasoning of language models.

items.loc: train.jsonl (7,473 lines) and test.jsonl (1,319 lines), counted here on 2026-11-15

protocol.v: the final answer is the number after #### on the last line of a solution; a problem is solved when that number, with commas removed, equals the reference

data_hash.loc: the file at commit 3101c7d, hashed here on 2026-11-15

versions.name: GSM8K (test set)

data.location: grade_school_math/data/test.jsonl of github.com/openai/grade-school-math at commit 3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c

protocol.scorer: exact match of the final number after ####, commas removed (grade_school_math/dataset.py); the shots, the prompt and the sampling differ from report to report and are in the setting of each result
protocol.unit: solved problems / all problems

ceiling.note: the authors estimate that less than 2 percent of problems contain breaking errors (Section 2); vendrow-2025-large-language-model judged 26 of 300 sampled test questions poorly written and 1 mislabeled (Table 2)

versions.known_issues: the paper rounds the sizes to 7.5K train and 1K test (Section 2), for 7,473 and 1,319 in the files; zhang-2024-careful-examination-large finds accuracy drops of up to 8% on GSM1k, new problems in the style of GSM8K, and signs that some models partly memorized GSM8K (abstract)

name: ARC-AGI-2
summary: The harder successor of ARC-AGI: grid puzzles calibrated on human testers, in which a system infers a transformation from a few examples and applies it to new inputs.

splits.v: public training (1,000), public evaluation (120), semi-private (120), private (120)

protocol.v: a task is solved when all its test outputs are exactly right, with 2 trials for each test input

data_hash.loc: a manifest of data/evaluation hashed here on 2026-11-15: one line '<sha256 of the file>  <file name>' a file, sorted by name, then the sha256 of the manifest

versions.name: ARC-AGI-2 (public evaluation set)

size.loc: 120 files with 167 test inputs, counted here on 2026-11-15

data.location: data/evaluation of github.com/arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49

protocol.scorer: exact match of each output grid, 2 trials a test input (README, Task success criterion; the section Task file format of the same README says 3)
protocol.unit: solved tasks / all tasks

human_baseline.note: the average human performance on the public evaluation tasks; each task was solved by at least 2 people in 2 attempts or fewer (README); Epoch AI's page says 60%

versions.known_issues: the public evaluation tasks changed after the release: 21 on 2025-04-14 and 1 on 2025-04-17 (changelog.md), and 5 more on 2025-05-15 that the changelog does not list, so a result must name its commit; 6 ids of the public evaluation set are also ids of the ARC-AGI-1 evaluation set, with other content
